sources.locator: "Murder of the Romanov family", revision 1374973698, lead

explanation: The execution’s own lead begins the family’s captivity at the revolution. The article reads: "Following the February Revolution in 1917, the Romanovs and their servants had been imprisoned in the Alexander Palace before being moved to Tobolsk, Siberia, in the aftermath of the October Revolution."

retraction.reason: A14(4): one of the eleven A13 edges whose quote opens "Following", "After" or "In the aftermath", re-read under the fire's own refusal class — chronology with no claim in it. A13 asks for an edge where the article states that one event caused, enabled, preceded or reacted to the other, and here the sentence says the Romanovs "had been imprisoned in the Alexander Palace" following the revolution. That the captivity followed the revolution is stated; that the execution followed from it is not. The article opens its account there and the edge read the opening as an argument. The quote stays in this record; what is withdrawn is the claim that the article made the link.
